question: What is the primary function of the autonomic nervous system?
explanation: The autonomic nervous system specifically manages visceral and involuntary functions to maintain stable internal conditions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h1)

question: How does the autonomic nervous system differ fundamentally from the somatic nervous system?

options.A: Somatic pathways innervate internal visceral organs
options.B: Autonomic pathways operate without conscious control
options.C: Somatic pathways regulate smooth muscle automatically
options.D: Autonomic pathways exclusively use single motor neurons

explanation: Voluntary movement is governed by the somatic system, whereas visceral activities regulated by the autonomic system happen automatically. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h1)

question: Where do preganglionic neurons of the sympathetic nervous system originate?

options.A: Peripheral ganglia near target visceral organs
options.B: Craniosacral region of the central nervous system
options.C: Thoracolumbar region of the spinal cord
options.D: Cerebral cortex and basal ganglia regions

explanation: Sympathetic outflow arises specifically from the thoracic and lumbar segments of the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which physiological response is characteristic of the parasympathetic division?

options.A: Dilation of bronchial airways in lungs

explanation: The rest-and-digest division enhances gastrointestinal activity, whereas sympathetic activation suppresses digestion. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which neurotransmitter is released by all autonomic preganglionic nerve fibers?
explanation: Acetylcholine serves as the primary neurotransmitter at all autonomic ganglia for both sympathetic and parasympathetic systems. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h3)

question: What type of receptors are found on target organs of the parasympathetic nervous system?
explanation: Parasympathetic postganglionic terminals release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors located on effector tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the effect of sympathetic nervous system activation on the bronchi of the lungs?
explanation: Sympathetic stimulation widens airway passages to maximize oxygen intake during high-demand physical exertion. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h4)

question: A patient presents to the emergency department experiencing severe sympathetic activation. Which physical sign is most likely to be observed?
explanation: Fight-or-flight activation drives up the heart rate and opens the pupils to gather more light in perceived danger. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which structure is considered the master controller of the autonomic nervous system within the brain?
explanation: The hypothalamus integrates visceral inputs and commands autonomic reflexes alongside hormonal secretion. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is a key characteristic of the enteric nervous system?

options.A: It functions exclusively as part of the sympathetic division
options.B: It has no neurons located inside the wall of the intestines
options.C: It can operate semi-independently to control gastrointestinal functions
options.D: It relies entirely on direct signals from the cerebral cortex

explanation: The enteric nervous system manages local gut movements and secretions even if neural connections to the brain are severed. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which common chronic disease frequently leads to peripheral autonomic neuropathy?
explanation: Chronic hyperglycemia damages autonomic nerve fibers over time, resulting in diverse visceral complications. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h6)

question: What triggers the dangerous blood pressure spike known as autonomic dysreflexia in spinal cord injury patients?

options.A: Complete failure of the adrenal glands to release cortisol
options.B: Direct parasympathetic hyperstimulation from the brainstem
options.C: Noxious sensory stimuli below the level of the spinal lesion
options.D: Excessive circulating levels of acetylcholine in the blood

explanation: Bladder distension or pressure sores trigger unmodulated sympathetic reflexes below the injury, causing dangerous vasoconstriction. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h6)
